title: SDK Retry Heuristics, Stream Resumption Tokens, and Idempotency Key Playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Author a practical, language-targeted playbook that defines sane defaults for retry/backoff behavior across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs; specifies stream resumption token semantics; and prescribes idempotency key lifecycle, rotation, and telemetry hooks. This ticket produces a single canonical doc + language-specific appendices and example snippets to ship with SDK releases.
problem_statement: Current SDK implementations have slightly different retry defaults, inconsistent idempotency key guidance, and unclear expectations for resuming interrupted streaming responses. This causes customer confusion, duplicated support work, and subtle production failures in high-latency or partially-connected environments.
goals: Define cross-SDK default retry profile(s) appropriate for hosted and dedicated deployments
Standardize idempotency key semantics: TTL, key rotation, and server-side acceptance guarantees
Specify stream resumption contract (resume tokens vs request replay) and example APIs for resumable streams
Provide pragmatic per-language ergonomics and code examples for Python/TS/Go
Surface telemetry/span hooks and metrics to help diagnose retry storms and duplicate work
non_goals: Change server-side acceptance semantics (this is a client guidance doc)
Implement SDK changes in this ticket — implementation tracked in follow-ups
proposed_solution: Deliver a playbook that prescribes two retry profiles (Conservative and Aggressive), an exponential backoff with full jitter formula default, an idempotency key model with 24-hour soft TTL and 30-day archival retention for reconciliation, and a small resume-token surface for streaming APIs. Include sample wrappers for sync/async patterns in Python and TS and goroutine-safe helpers in Go. Provide configuration knobs (max_attempts, base_delay_ms, max_delay_ms, jitter_strategy) and clear guidance on when to opt out (e.g., non-idempotent side effects).
decision_records: Choose exponential backoff + full jitter (AWS-style) as default to minimize thundering herd
Default max_attempts = 3 for Conservative, 6 for Aggressive (sensible for retries that are idempotent or safely resumable)
Streaming resumption: prefer resume token when server provides it; otherwise clients should support partial-request replay up to configured max bytes/retries
Idempotency key ttl: server should accept keys for 24h for deduplication; clients should retain keys locally for 48h for retries; rotation every 30d for long-lived keys
Telemetry: SDKs must emit retry_count, last_retry_backoff_ms, idempotency_key_used, stream_resumed boolean, and a span/event on final failure
tradeoffs: Longer idempotency TTL reduces duplicate work but increases server storage; 24h chosen as pragmatic balance
Aggressive retry profile reduces visible latency for transient infra errors but increases cost and risk of duplicate side-effects if misused
Resume-token surface adds complexity to server-side implementation and client code but provides deterministic stream resumption in most cases
acceptance_criteria: Playbook doc reviewed and approved by SDK leads for Python, TS, and Go
Language appendices include copy-paste examples for sync/async variants
Additions to SDK telemetry spec reviewed by Observability team
Follow-up implementation tickets created for each SDK with clear PR checklist items

implementation_notes: Expose a RetryConfig struct/object with fields: max_attempts:int, base_delay_ms:int, max_delay_ms:int, jitter_strategy:string, retryable_error_codes:list
Provide helper: should_retry(err, attempt_count, idempotency_key_present) to centralize logic
Streaming client: resume() should accept resume_token and return a resumed stream object; SDKs must document when token is unavailable and fallback semantics
Idempotency helper: generate_key(user_provided_key=None) uses HMAC(SPAN_ID || timestamp || nonce) if server requires key signature
Add unit + integration tests simulating transient network failures, server 5xx, and duplicate acceptance to verify deduplication
language_guidance: Python: provide sync and asyncio wrappers. Async should expose retry as an async context manager for easy use with streaming iterators.
TypeScript: provide both callback and async-iterator ergonomics; document browser vs Node considerations for local key persistence (IndexedDB vs filesystem).
Go: prefer context-aware functions with small, concurrency-safe RetryClient; demonstrate patterns for goroutine-shared idempotency key stores.
error_taxonomy: Retryable transient: connection timeouts, ECONNRESET, transient DNS failures, 502/503 with Retry-After absent or short — allowed for Conservative profile
Retryable safe: idempotent operation recognized by idempotency key or storage-backed resume token — allowed for Aggressive profile
Non-retryable permanent: 4xx client errors indicating bad input, 401/403 (auth), 422 (invalid content) — should fail fast
Ambiguous server errors: 500 with side-effect unknown — default to Conservative (single automatic retry), require explicit idempotency key for additional retries
streaming_contract: Resume token must be opaque to clients; server guarantees that supplying the token will continue stream deterministically from the last acked position
Clients must include idempotency_key when starting a stream if they expect server-side deduplication on reconnect
If resume token unavailable, clients may replay from last known user-visible checkpoint; SDK should provide helpers to stitch partial results
Recommend server include: resume_token, last_committed_offset, and optional estimated_remaining_bytes in stream preface
observability_and_metrics: Mandatory metrics: sdk.retry.count{profile}, sdk.retry.backoff_ms.p50/p95, sdk.idempotency.dup_attempts, sdk.stream.resume_attempts
Logs: warning on >3 automatic retries in Conservative profile, error on final failure with full retry history
testing_plan: Unit tests for backoff math and jitter behavior
Integration tests simulating flaky connections using network fault injection harness
Chaos run: enable aggressive profile against staging with injected 502s to measure duplicate effects
E2E: validate resume tokens by truncating streaming responses mid-flight and ensuring resume returns identical payload sequence

notes_for_engineers: Avoid adding retries around user-supplied callbacks that cause side-effects unless idempotency is explicit
Document clear opt-out path: e.g., RetryConfig.enable = false
Ensure SDK default logs are informative but not verbose for regular retries (use rate-limited warnings)
